Definition: from the base of G5494; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt:--dust.
BiblicalUsage: Choos is a heap, loose dirt or rubbish poured out, and the Greek text knows it under the spelling for dust. The disciples are told to shake off the dust under their feet against a town that will not receive them, and the merchants of the earth cast dust on their heads weeping over fallen Babylon. The Greek text spells the word as dust rather than the dictionary form, so both verses are cited as a spelling variant rather than an exact match.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the dust shaken off and the dust cast on the head are two sides of one judgment, because the same dust marks rejection and ruin.
